raw_record.support_text: In this double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of rimegepant 75 mg oral tablet versus placebo for acute migraine treatment, the authors state: 'No signal of drug-induced liver injury due to rimegepant was identified.' The conclusion reiterates that tolerability and safety were similar to placebo with no evidence of hepatotoxicity. This is an explicit agent-specific negative conclusion about human drug-induced liver injury for rimegepant.
raw_record.extra_details: Rimegepant 75 mg oral tablet, a small molecule CGRP receptor antagonist, in acute migraine treatment. Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled phase trial (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03235479); 1485 enrolled, 1162 randomized (rimegepant n=582; placebo n=580), mostly female (85.5%), mean age 41.6 years. Coprimary endpoints: pain freedom and most bothersome symptom freedom at 2 h postdose. No DILI signal and no evidence of hepatotoxicity reported.

condition_text: Treatment in children (median age at start 3.9 years, range 0.3-13.1) with primary bile acid synthesis defects (3β-hydroxy-Δ⁵-C₂₇-steroid oxidoreductase [3β-HSD] or Δ⁴-3-oxosteroid 5β-reductase [Δ⁴-3-oxo-R] deficiency).

raw_record.support_text: The paper states that cholic acid (CA) is now recognized as the bile acid of choice for 3β-HSD and Δ⁴-3-oxo-R deficiencies because it is not hepatotoxic and is effective therapy, and concludes that prolonged oral CA therapy is safe. This is supported by prospective follow-up of 15 children with primary bile acid synthesis defects (initial mean dose 13 mg/kg, 6 mg/kg at last evaluation, median treatment follow-up 12.4 years) in which serum liver biochemistries and sonography normalized and post-treatment liver biopsies showed marked improvement, with CA tolerated well.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Treatment in children (median age at start 3.9 years, range 0.3-13.1) with primary bile acid synthesis defects (3β-hydroxy-Δ⁵-C₂₇-steroid oxidoreductase [3β-HSD] or Δ⁴-3-oxosteroid 5β-reductase [Δ⁴-3-oxo-R] deficiency).
raw_record.extra_details: 15 patients (13 with 3β-HSD, 2 twin sisters with Δ⁴-3-oxo-R deficiency) from 10 families, followed prospectively from 1993 to 2007 at Bicêtre Hospital. Liver biopsies after at least 5 years of CA therapy in 14 patients showed marked improvement, especially in 3β-HSD deficiency. Atypical urinary metabolites reduced 500-fold (3β-HSD) and 30-fold (Δ⁴-3-oxo-R). Two women had normal pregnancies during treatment. Study aimed to assess long-term effectiveness and safety of oral cholic acid; the paper explicitly asserts CA is not hepatotoxic (vs. chenodeoxycholic acid also used for bile acid replacement).

raw_record.support_text: The study concluded: 'There was no association between rifampicin concentrations and hepatotoxicity or isoniazid concentrations and peripheral neuropathy among TB/HIV-coinfected patients.' In the cohort, participants with no, mild, moderate, or severe hepatotoxicity had median rifampicin Cmax values of 6.57, 7.39, 7.00, and 3.86 µg/mL respectively, with no difference in median rifampicin Cmax between those with and without hepatotoxicity (P = 0.322).
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: TB/HIV-coinfected patients on standard-dose anti-TB treatment according to WHO guidelines
raw_record.extra_details: Prospective cohort of 268 patients (58% male, median age 34). Hepatotoxicity graded using Division of AIDS toxicity tables. Cox regression used to assess association between rifampicin Cmax (measured by HPLC at 1, 2, and 4 h after drug intake at 2, 8, and 24 weeks) and hepatotoxicity; no association found (P = 0.322).

raw_record.support_text: The paper reports no appreciable increase in hepatic enzymes with conversion from simvastatin to atorvastatin, and no significant differences in alanine aminotransferase or aspartate aminotransferase were seen in either statin group. No drug-induced liver injury is attributed to simvastatin in this cohort; the reported adverse event was rhabdomyolysis (muscle toxicity).
raw_record.extra_details: Observational lipid-clinic cohort (group A n=841, group B n=104). No significant differences in ALT or AST vs atorvastatin. The main statin-related adverse event was rhabdomyolysis (CK ~18,000-32,000 U/L in 3 group B patients), all but 1 case occurring at 80 mg simvastatin; physicians advised awareness of increased rhabdomyolysis risk at 80 mg simvastatin. No hepatic injury was attributed to simvastatin.

condition_text: Inadvertent paracetamol overdose in a setting of self-medication during flu, with concurrent over-the-counter flu remedies and a relative's Tylex capsules (which also contain paracetamol); hepato-renal failure and fulminant hepatic failure.

raw_record.support_text: A 48-year-old female presented with clouded consciousness and weakness after seven days of flu symptoms; she had been taking paracetamol, over-the-counter flu remedies and a relative's Tylex capsules. She was diagnosed with hepato-renal failure secondary to paracetamol overdose, with ALT >10,000, bilirubin 121 micromol/l, INR 6.0 and a low paracetamol level (0.1 mmol/l). Despite resuscitation she died within two hours of admission to ICU; the cause of death was fulminant hepatic failure secondary to inadvertent paracetamol overdose.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Inadvertent paracetamol overdose in a setting of self-medication during flu, with concurrent over-the-counter flu remedies and a relative's Tylex capsules (which also contain paracetamol); hepato-renal failure and fulminant hepatic failure.
raw_record.extra_details: Comorbid decompensation: jaundice, dehydration, rigid abdomen, metabolic acidosis (pH 7.15), hypoglycemia (glucose 0.5 mmol/l), renal impairment (creatinine 251 micromol/l), coagulopathy (INR 6.0, prothrombin time 62.3 s); paracetamol level 0.1 mmol/l; death occurred within two hours of ICU admission. Discussion frames this as danger of self-medication with commonly available over-the-counter drugs.

condition_text: High-dose therapy as part of the CTC (cyclophosphamide, thiotepa, carboplatin) chemotherapy regimen for refractory germ-cell cancer and metastatic breast cancer; VOD occurred after second courses.

raw_record.support_text: The goal of this study was to assess the impact of exposure to bioactivated cyclophosphamide on the occurrence of veno-occlusive disease (VOD, hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome) caused by the high-dose CTC chemotherapy regimen. The authors found that increased first-course exposures to 4-hydroxycyclophosphamide led to increased occurrence of VOD in 4 of 59 patients. The discussion notes that hepatic injury from high-dose cyclophosphamide has been reported to be cyclophosphamide dose-related.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: High-dose therapy as part of the CTC (cyclophosphamide, thiotepa, carboplatin) chemotherapy regimen for refractory germ-cell cancer and metastatic breast cancer; VOD occurred after second courses.
raw_record.extra_details: 4/59 patients developed VOD (3 with refractory germ-cell cancer after a second CTC course; 1 with metastatic breast cancer after a second tCTC course). Significant relationship between first-course 4-hydroxycyclophosphamide AUC and VOD (P=0.003); mean first-course 4-hydroxycyclophosphamide AUC was 134.5 microM h in patients without VOD vs 184.5 microM h in those with VOD. Phosphoramide mustard AUC not significant (P=0.101; means 526.7 vs 792.0 microM h). No significant relationship between total cumulative 4-hydroxycyclophosphamide or phosphoramide mustard AUC and VOD (P=0.173 and 0.428). Hepatic injury reported dose-related (Honjo 1988). Mechanistic roles proposed for acrolein (binding to cytochrome enzymes, hepatic macromolecules, nucleic acids; glutathione depletion) and for glutathione-S-transferase inhibition; busulphan-induced glutathione depletion in bone-marrow transplantation combination also noted.

raw_record.support_text: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) overdose is described as a leading cause of acute liver failure (ALF), and when patients fulfill the King's College criteria for acetaminophen-induced ALF (AALF) they have a poor prognosis for survival without liver transplantation.
raw_record.extra_details: Case of a 41-year-old female with no documented history of liver disease who presented with acute acetaminophen toxicity and developed hepatic encephalopathy, coagulopathy and lactic acidosis; she met King's College criteria for liver transplantation based on pH and INR but was deemed not suitable due to psychosocial comorbidities. Treated with single-pass albumin dialysis (SPAD) starting day 3 of ICU admission for five consecutive daily runs (~77 hours) as a bridge to recovery; course complicated by cerebral edema requiring mannitol. Native liver function recovered by hospital discharge (day 46), with bilirubin <100 mmol/L; no long-term neurological sequelae.

raw_record.support_text: The paper reports a young man with a previously unrecognized POLG-1 mutation who developed valproic acid-associated acute liver failure and was treated successfully with liver transplantation. It also notes that patients with POLG-1 gene mutations have an increased risk of valproic acid-induced acute liver failure, that severe valproate hepatotoxicity most commonly arises in children within the first 3 months of treatment with an estimated incidence of 1 in 40,000 treated patients, and that many experts consider valproic acid-induced acute liver failure in patients with mitochondrial disorders a contraindication to liver transplant due to high mortality among transplanted children.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Patient was a young man harboring a previously unrecognized POLG-1 gene mutation (mitochondrial disorder), which increases the risk of valproic acid-induced acute liver failure; report is a single case successfully managed with liver transplantation.
raw_record.extra_details: Acute liver failure explicitly reported; severe valproate hepatotoxicity most commonly arises in children within the first 3 months of treatment, with an estimated overall incidence of 1 in 40,000 treated patients; high mortality among transplanted children underlies expert consideration of valproic acid-induced acute liver failure in mitochondrial disorders as a contraindication to liver transplant; case treated successfully with liver transplantation. Aliases: valproate, VPA.

raw_record.support_text: Most POLG patients in the cohort only needed a transplant due to liver failure iatrogenically triggered by initiation of valproic acid. The authors describe this as one clearly preventable cause of irreversible liver failure and advise restraint in starting patients with unexplained epilepsy on valproate. Five patients in the cohort had POLG-related Alpers-Huttenlocher syndrome (AHS) disease with valproate-induced liver failure, two of whom had no post-transplant complications.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Occurred in patients with POLG-related mitochondrial disease (POLG-related Alpers-Huttenlocher syndrome, AHS); patients required liver transplantation for irreversible liver failure; note of caution needed before proceeding with liver transplant in this specific mitochondrial disease.
raw_record.extra_details: Five of the cohort's patients with POLG-related AHS had valproate-induced liver failure; two of five had no post-transplant complications or disease worsening. Valproic acid initiation framed as iatrogenic trigger; valproate also referred to by name 'valproate'. The indication was management of unexplained epilepsy.

raw_record.support_text: Blood microRNA was analyzed in capillary blood of RUCAM-based cases with intrinsic drug-induced liver injury (DILI) caused by acetaminophen (APAP) overdoses. The text notes that most microRNA biomarkers have been described for human intrinsic DILI caused by APAP overdoses, establishing that APAP overdose causes intrinsic DILI in humans, while clarifying that the exosomes' diagnostic or mechanistic role in human intrinsic DILI by APAP remains to be established.
raw_record.extra_details: Blood microRNA was analyzed in capillary blood of RUCAM-Based cases with intrinsic DILI caused by APAP. Exosomes are released into the blood from livers of mice treated with acetaminophen (N-acetyl-p-aminophenol; APAP) leading to experimental intrinsic DILI, but their diagnostic or mechanistic role in human intrinsic DILI by APAP remains to be established.
